issues.description: The problem statement contains two conflicting specifications for the milk method signature: the UML and several tasks define messageOnMilk() with no parameters, while a later paragraph (Part 2) requires messageOnMilk(double milkVolume). The solution and template use a no-argument messageOnMilk(), but the textual requirement asking for a double parameter would lead students to implement a different signature and return format (including volume). This mismatch will confuse students about the correct interface method signature and will cause implementation/tests to fail if they follow the contradictory textual instruction.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the required signature for the milk method consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement (Part 2 text) to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and adjust the example return string to not include a volume, matching the UML, template, and solution; or (B) change the Milkable interface, all implementations, and template calls to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update the UML and tests accordingly so every artifact expects the same parameterized signature and return format.

issues.description: The expected signature and behavior of messageOnMilk is inconsistent across the artifacts: the narrative Part 2 of the problem statement requires messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and specifies a return string including the volume, whereas the UML, the example Main usage, the template/solution implementations, and the Milkable interface use messageOnMilk() with no parameter and return strings without a volume. This mismatch creates direct confusion about which method signature students must implement and what the output should contain.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the signature inconsistency by choosing one contract and applying it everywhere. Option A (preferred if volume tracking is required): change the Milkable interface to declare messageOnMilk(double milkVolume), update all implementations (Seal, Goat, etc.) to accept the double and return the string format "[Animal Type] [name] is milked (volume: [milkVolume]L)", and update all call sites (including Main and Farm tests) to pass a volume. Option B (if no volume is intended): update the problem statement Part 2 text to match the UML and implementations, specifying messageOnMilk() with no parameter and the return string without a volume. Ensure the UML, example Main, template stubs, and tests reflect the chosen signature.
